description: Closing call-to-action sections and mid-page CTA bands. On a trade site this is the last push to call, book or request an estimate. It should remove the remaining doubt (what happens next, how fast, do you serve me) and make the phone number tappable.
queries: home services call to action section
closing call to action section with background photo
get a free quote call to action band
navigation bar with phone number and call now button

references.layout: Cream paper page with print grain. A big serif headline spans the top. Left column: body paragraphs. Right column: a dashed-border coupon (~270×260) with a scissors icon on its left edge. Inside: serif 'Act now! Book a Consultation.', instructions to 'Cut along the dotted line and mail this', an 'Email: ____' underline field, a 3-line postal address, 'Or click below.', and a full-width dark brown button with a phone glyph, 'Book a Call Today'. The nav has an underlined '☎ Book a call'.
references.type: Old-style serif (Cheltenham / Century feel) throughout. Headline ~48px, coupon heading ~16px bold, body ~13px. No sans at all.
references.color: Paper ~#EFE6D2, ink brown ~#3E352B, button ~#3B3127, dashed rule in ink. Slight halftone/ink-bleed texture.
details: Dashed cut line with a scissors glyph, a literal coupon
Full postal address inside the CTA (a trust signal)
Phone glyph on the button and in the nav
Print grain makes the whole page feel like a mailer
references.why_it_works: It's witty and tactile, and it uses the native language of trade marketing (door hangers, mailers, clip-out coupons).
references.trade_adaptation: '$50 OFF ANY REPAIR: show this to your technician' coupon with dashed border, licence number, street address and a '☎ Call (555) 012-3456' button. Fits plumbers, HVAC, pest control and garage doors.

references.layout: Left: a bold 2-line headline and a paragraph on light gray. Right: a masonry grid of 6+ photos of people at services. A white card (~260px) overlaps the center of the grid: heading 'Ready to learn more?', two icon rows (clipboard: 'Fill out our quote form (in less than 5 minutes)'; clock: 'Get a response within 1-2 business days'), a full-width blue 'Request a quote' button, and an underlined alternative link 'Not sure if ClassPass is right for you? Take our quiz.'
references.type: Sans bold ~24px headline, ~18px card heading, ~12px rows.
references.color: Blue ~#1F5BFF, white card with soft shadow, gray ~#F4F4F4 panel, full-color photos.
details: Sets expectations: how long the form takes and when they'll reply
Offers a lower-commitment path (quiz) under the main button
The card overlaps the photo grid, so proof surrounds the ask
references.why_it_works: It answers the biggest lead-form worry, 'what happens after I click?', in two lines.
references.trade_adaptation: Card over a grid of job photos: 'Get your free estimate' / 'Two-minute form' / 'We call back within 2 business hours' / [Request estimate] / 'Prefer to talk? (555) 012-3456'.

references.layout: Left: a 3-line heavy uppercase headline 'GET PRICING TAILORED TO YOUR PROPERTY', a 3-step checklist (✓ bold step title + gray one-line description), and at the bottom award badges with year chips ('2024 2025 2026'). Right: a compact form (2-column first/last name, email, country + phone, selects, an optional free-text field), privacy microcopy and a full-width pink pill 'GET PRICING'.

details: The steps explain the process right beside the form
Award badges carry year chips, showing repeated wins
Placeholder labels inside fields keep the form compact
references.why_it_works: Persuasion (steps and awards) and action (form) share one screen, so nobody has to scroll between them.
references.trade_adaptation: 'GET A QUOTE FOR YOUR ROOF' with steps 'Tell us about your home / Free on-site inspection / Written quote in 48 hrs', badges 'BBB A+', 'Angi Super Service 2024 2025', a manufacturer certification. Form: name, phone, address, service select.

Below, a hairline line-drawing of the US with state outlines, + markers, thin circles and colored arcs connecting locations.

references.color: Cream ~#FFF5E8, ink ~#111111, hairlines ~#CFC6B8, arc accents orange ~#F26B1D, amber ~#F7B733, lavender ~#B9A6F5.

The service-area map is drawn in hairlines, not a Google embed
A small, square button under a big serif headline shows restraint

references.trade_adaptation: 'See if we serve your street' + a hairline county map with + markers on served towns and a ring around the shop location.

'Based in' answers locality
'No commitment' sits as quiet gray reassurance

references.layout: Cream section. Left: a rounded (~12px) landscape photo (~48% width) of the product installed in green hills. Right, vertically centered: a 2-line condensed uppercase headline and a small black pill 'Get in touch ↗'.

The photo shows the product in place, in context
The headline speaks to the visitor's situation: 'fits with your business'

references.trade_adaptation: Garage-door company: photo of an installed door on a craftsman house, 'SEE HOW A NEW DOOR CHANGES YOUR CURB APPEAL.' + 'Get a quote ↗'.

Lowercase voice feels conversational

references.trade_adaptation: 'let's get your [Book a tune-up →] furnace ready for winter' or 'need it fixed [Call now →] today?'.

references.layout: Black section. Rounded (~16px) photos of real small-business owners and workers (café, retail, warehouse, tattooed shop owner) are scattered at varied sizes around the edges and cropped by the viewport. Centered: small caps kicker 'WHY SQUARE?', a 2-line white headline, a blue filled and a blue outline button.

Real customers of many types

references.layout: White section. A one-line lead-in question (~11px) sits above a 3-line centered condensed caps headline. Below are two square-cornered buttons: tan filled 'Book an appointment to get started' and an outlined 'See our services & solutions'.

The headline is a process promise, not a slogan
Long, descriptive button labels

references.trade_adaptation: 'Leak? Remodel? New build? We handle it start to finish.' / 'THREE VISITS. ONE PRICE. NO SURPRISES.' / [Book a free walkthrough] [See our services].

references.layout: Near-black section. A huge left-aligned 'Take the next step.' (~56px), a 2-line subhead (~22px) and an outline pill 'Get in touch'. Below are three columns, each with a thin line icon (laptop, people, $), a 2-line bold heading and blue links ('Shop for your small business.', 'Get service and support.', 'Explore financing options.'), plus plain text 'Call us at 1-800-854-3680.'

The phone number appears as plain text plus a link
Thin outline icons, not filled blobs

references.layout: A full-bleed band (~100px) above the footer. Centered 2-line white headline addressing a segment ('Restaurant groups: call to get the full picture…'), then a red button whose label is the phone number: 'CALL (866) 951-7154'. The footer repeats the number large in its right column.
references.color: Gradient navy ~#1E1446 to coral ~#D24B4B (generic; replace with a solid brand color), button red ~#D8423F.
details: The phone number IS the button label, so it is tap-to-call on mobile
The number is repeated in the footer for scanners
The headline names who should call
references.why_it_works: Direct and mobile-first. The gradient is the weak part; the phone-as-label move is the lesson.
references.trade_adaptation: 'Burst pipe or no heat? We answer 24/7.' [CALL (555) 012-3456] on a solid deep-red or navy band.

takeaways: Set expectations right next to the button: how long the form takes, when they'll hear back, what the first step is (ClassPass, Mews, Cloudstudio). This is the strongest conversion pattern found.
Make the phone number a tap-to-call button label, and repeat it as plain text nearby.
Phrase the CTA around the visitor's home or situation: 'See if your house qualifies', 'fits with your business', 'Leak? Remodel? New build?'
Put proof inside or around the ask: award badges with years, a hairline service-area map, real customer and job photos framing the headline.
Print metaphors make a trade site feel warm and local: dashed coupon borders, paper grain, old-style serif, clip-out offers.
Use one band color (or cream paper) with either light big type or heavy condensed caps. A small pill is enough when the headline carries the weight.
Offer a lower-commitment alternative under the main action ('Prefer to talk?', 'Not sure? Take the quiz').
avoid: Two-tone gradient bands (OpenTable 'Let's do this', Aboard purple) and pastel gradient cards with '$0/month' (Contra).
'Ready to get started?' + two equal buttons on pale gray with nothing else (Stripe, Dovetail 'Get in touch', Contra 'Try Contra today').
Empty black strips like 'Let's talk business' + a tiny button (UGLYCASH).
Random decorative shapes or 3D blobs around the headline (Figma, Ada pixel grid).
Darkened stock-photo bands with a centered white headline and one orange button (Eventbrite, Canva, Wix Learn).
Textured gradient paint backgrounds that fight the type (Wise 'CONTACT US TODAY').
